findings.title: Legacy-pin native 2P result phase (raw 7E:009F 0x84) lasts 35 frames where the original lasts 34 (bsnes-accurate, Snes9x, Beetle)

reproducer.command: python3 tools/qa_frontier_original_crosscheck.py paired --native-exe <Modern candidate> --seed 50036056 --arm rotation --lag 2 --finish-hold 4000 --frames 1128-1140,1620-4800/60,4801-6400 --snesref ... --core <snes9x|beetle> --ledger <ledger.json> --work W --out R

source_artifacts: Hosted run 38637954243 (research-race-relative-paired, main 08e454e, artifact research-race-relative-paired, receipt SHA-bound)
findings.observation: 49 seeds, measured lag 2 in all: decoded source fields identical through laps-zero (same frame in 49/49) and until the reference's 0x16 restoration; result-menu onset on the same frame in 43, one frame earlier on native in 6; scheduler parity at onset does not predict the outcome. Raw semantic WRAM ($0200+) first differs 1-2 native frames BEFORE result-menu (0x84) onset in 49 of 49 seeds (all five arms). For 50036056 at native 5196-5198 the original builds the sound-command queue at 7E:2000 (wSndQueueRead/Write/ApuToggle, serviced by 82:8035 inside the 80:FAC9 wait) in one frame (first word 01->02->04); native shows a different intermediate one frame later (01->03->04). 7E:0BDE/0BFE start at 0xCC->0xC8 on the original but 0xC4->0xC0 on native, an offset of 8 held through the whole phase. The 0x84 phase then lasts 34 frames on Snes9x (and on Beetle-bsnes for 50036056) and 35 on native in 48 of 49 (36 for 50024003). Per-core boundaries differ: Snes9x onset same frame in 43 and native one earlier in 6, with the restore later on native; Beetle-bsnes (50036056) onset native 5198 vs 5199, both restore 5233. 7E:009F is the DrawText cursor wTextPos (#1543), so 0x84->0x16 is a raw terminal signature. Adjudicated on the high-accuracy bsnes core (with tools/patches/bsnes-libretro-system-ram.patch): 34 frames in 9 of 9 seeds, matching Snes9x. See RF-015 for the product core, which errs the other way. Independent hosted re-execution (run 38637954243, three seeds, Snes9x and Beetle): entry 1136/1134, lag confirmed; 0x84 phase 35/34 (50012000, 50036056) and 36/34 (50024003) on both cores.
findings.uncertainty: Local candidate evidence (current-main native 4c1c8b56...) until independently re-executed with raw-dump receipts. 83:987D Sram_RestoreDirectPage is a downstream 207-word SRAM->DP copy, not a proven diverging decision. Gameplay significance pending the upstream caller and actual 7E:009F writer on each core. 7E:2000-2004 is the SPC700 sound-command queue (Baldosa RAM map; 82:8035 reads $2142); 7E:0BDE/0BFE is unnamed; whether the 8-unit offset is guest-visible (sprite Y or banner position) or only scheduling is unproven. 2026-10-14: the 7E:2000 queue step at 5196 also differs between Snes9x and bsnes, so it is not by itself evidence of a native defect.
findings.resolving_experiment: Measure the legacy pin's arrival line at the post-load 80:FAC9 wait and matched 82:B1DD upload checkpoint drift against Snes9x (the RF-015 method). The 5196 sound-queue step is phase-sensitive between correct cores (Snes9x vs bsnes) and cannot localize a defect by itself. cd5875c carries the same refresh-rate code as Baldosa yet errs long, so its larger beam/$4212 deficit (RF-014) dominates.
findings.consequence: A cheap deterministic 2P reproducer of the same result-handoff seam behind the open 1P Switcher +4704/+4702 strict divergence; it does not change any comparator or acceptance.

reproducer.command: stock tests/input/two-player-first-race.input on Snes9x and the Modern native, dump every 4 host frames 2..1126, count decrements of 7E:00C6 (one per 80:FAC9 vblank-wait pass via 80:FADF)

source_artifacts: reference/imported/reverse-engineering/nitrodon/bank 80.txt 80:FAC9-80:FAF9 (LDA $4212 BMI/BPL wait; DEC $C6 mod 32; STA $0BDE/$0BFE from table 80:FBAF)
generic setup_project native (fda6ace framework pin), same census: 772 game frames
bsnes-libretro high-accuracy core (tools/toolchain.json pin 05439f96) agrees with Snes9x on every blank-screen run
Hosted run 38637954243 (research-race-relative-paired, main 08e454e, artifact research-race-relative-paired, receipt SHA-bound)
findings.observation: Over host frames 2-1126: native 773 FAC9 passes, Snes9x 801, Beetle-bsnes 802 (two independent reference cores agree within one frame). Both engines run one pass per host frame in steady menus. Native loses passes only in transition/slide windows (menus 0x84, 0xD7, 0x3D, 0x6D, 0x91; e.g. host 442-446: native 0, original 4). The resulting 7E:00C6 offset of 4 (mod 32) is frozen during the race and explains RF-012's 7E:0BDE/0BFE offset of 8 exactly (0BDE = table[C6>>1]). A generic SNESRecomp native built by setup_project without the Modern product patches completes 772 game frames, so the deficit is in the shared framework/generated-code timing, not the Modern host. One-frame localisation of the 0x84->0xD7 transition: all engines hold 7E:00C6 at 0x02 from host 426 (a load); Snes9x resumes decrementing at 437 and Beetle at 436, native at 442; menu 0xD7 appears at 440 on both reference cores and at 446 on native. The no-input attract cycle (host 2-4002, one counter-rewrite window excluded) shows the same deficit: native 1311 passes, Snes9x 1326, Beetle-bsnes 1327. Player-visible confirmation (tools/qa_blank_screen_census.py, every frame, framebuffers only): on the stock 2P route the reference (bsnes-libretro high-accuracy = Snes9x; Beetle within one frame) shows black-screen runs 248-276, 401-443, 988-1150; native shows 248-278, 404-449, 988-1151 (+2, +3, +1). Attract cycle: +2, +3, +3, +2 with later loads starting 17 frames late by host 3632. 2P race-finish transition (seed 50036056): +1. Generic SNESRecomp build: +2, +3, 0. In the first load (reference 248-276) WRAM at $0200+ stays byte-identical between native and Snes9x while VRAM fills: the reference's VRAM fills by about 738 words per frame (measured VRAM progress; writer not identified by executed PC: 81:CD70-81:D09C came from a static search and is the race-HUD initializer per QA-01, while 82:B1D8 (Attract_Main/logo, STA $2118/$2119 at 82:B1F5/B1FC) and 81:BB89 Decomp_ToVram are stronger static candidates, #1566), native's VRAM progress falls 1 then 2 frames behind and converges at 278, so native completes the same VRAM upload work in about 7% more host frames. The second load (reference 401) starts later on native because the transition waits for the 7E:00C6 phase, which native reaches 4 frames later. Scope: the pinned Baldosa guest (gamesbyian/uniracers-recomp 10b864b, snesrecomp fork 075fbe4, executable c3471741...) matches the references within one frame on all five attract-cycle loads and completes 1327 vblank-wait passes (Beetle 1327, Snes9x 1326, legacy native 1311). The deficit belongs to this repo's snesrecomp pin cd5875c (current Modern build, generic build, frontier executable), not to the Baldosa fork being integrated. Independent hosted re-execution (run 38637954243): 773 native vs 801 Snes9x / 802 Beetle vblank-wait passes; black runs native 248-278, 404-449, 988-1151 vs bsnes 248-276, 401-443, 988-1150. Independent Baldosa hosted run 38644429519: Baldosa 801 vblank-wait passes (Snes9x 801, Beetle 802, legacy native 773); Baldosa black runs 248-276, 401-443, 988-1149 vs bsnes 248-276, 401-443, 988-1150 (legacy native 248-278, 404-449, 988-1151).
findings.uncertainty: Local candidate evidence until independently re-executed with raw receipts. Neither reference core is cycle-exact hardware, but they agree with each other and disagree with native by 28-29 frames. The source of native's deficit (host frame pacing, DMA/HDMA cost modelling or the $4212 model) is unknown; AGENTS forbids tuning $4212 merely to match one emulator. First suspect, unverified: the framework's synthetic $4212 beam model (snesrecomp pinned in tools/toolchain.json at cd5875cbdaf1 runner/src/snes/snes.c readReg 0x4212: fixed 64-clock advance per poll in static-recomp mode; docs/VIRTUAL_HW_CONTRACT.md), which sets how many host frames a polled load costs; upstream notes a sibling case (SMRPG boot fades at the wrong frame count). 7E:00C6 is wCursorAnimTimer in Baldosa's RAM map: it counts passes of this wait continuation, not simulation frames. The first-load writer, $420D/MEMSEL, M/X and CPU-vs-DMA path are unmeasured.
findings.resolving_experiment: QA-01 / native-fidelity: executed-PC histogram with $420D, M, $2118/$2119 write sequence, CPU cycles and vblank for host 248-278 on the reference, then compare snesrecomp cd5875c against Baldosa's fork 075fbe4 (96b7e9f $4212 read-time sync, b7b4318 paced_bus) for that writer; QA-01's MEMSEL model (#1562) predicts an old-pin per-store overcharge only if $420D=0.
findings.consequence: It leaves the shipping Windows path only for a nominated build proven to use the 075fbe4 fork; the default modern-shared-native-acceptance build recompiles against cd5875c. It still affects the legacy Modern backend kept as rollback, and any research run on the frontier executable: frontier frontend timing is not original timing, although the race itself is original-exact (RF-004). Likely common cause of RF-012 and RF-013 on the legacy pin; QA-01's Baldosa entry lags (+2/+1/+2) need a separate explanation.

findings.title: Baldosa runs the SPC700 at 17088 cycles per field (~1.02696 MHz) where Snes9x and bsnes use ~1.02528 MHz: SPC uploads end early, explaining the attract 941-1098 load and the remaining one-field-early 2P result onset (seed 50048000)

reproducer.command: python3 tools/qa_blank_screen_census.py --input <comment-only input> --snesref <snesref> --core <bsnes patched> --core <snes9x> --baldosa-exe <Baldosa 10b864b + research 2P shim [+ refresh patch]> --frames 240-290,395-455,935-1105,1415-1555,3625-3770 --allow-gaps --work W --out R

findings.observation: Low WRAM ($0200-$1DFF) is identical on Snes9x, bsnes and both Baldosa builds every frame 2-1096. The 941-1098 black load is Snd_UploadBlockList (82:82A9): 64 block headers via JSR $8328 and CPU decompression (82:812A) feeding a byte stream (82:82EF STA $2143/STA $2142, 82:8301 CMP $2142/BNE). All 46,414 port-2 writes align one-to-one by value; Baldosa gains ~19k master clocks during the IPL/handshake phase (1009-1025) and ~50k steadily across the ~71-field stream (655 vs 653-654 bytes per field), ending ~73k clocks (~54 lines) ahead. The black screen therefore ends at 1097 vs 1098 and the next starts at 1422 vs 1423; unaffected by the RF-015 refresh correction, which fixed the 3632-3762 load. The remaining 2P onset residual is the same mechanism: on seed 50048000 the original CPU is in the result-screen song upload (Snd_UploadBlockList) until 5013 V=230 and reaches 80:FAC9 at V=232, seven lines after VBlank; the refresh-corrected core onsets at 5014. With the disposable 17060-cycle build the paired run gives onset 5015 = 5015, 34 = 34 and one transient 7-byte frame (5012).
findings.uncertainty: Disposable A/B executed 2026-10-14 (refresh-corrected build + RTL_APU_CYCLES_PER_FRAME 17060, exe 81315543...): the 941 load then ends on bsnes's frame (1098) and the next starts on it (1423), but 1423-1548 vs 1547 and 3633-3763 vs 3632-3762 move one frame late. The SPC rate therefore participates, but the references' nominal 32040 Hz x 32 over-corrects other loads and the ~19k-clock IPL-phase lead is unattributed. Real consoles' APU resonators vary; Baldosa's audio pipeline is built around 534 samples per field, so the rate is a design constant, not a one-line fix. The RF-017 in-order register-access correction (2026-10-15) leaves every RF-016 witness unchanged: attract 941-1097/1422, 2P seed 50048000 at 5052, Switcher +4664. 2026-10-15: rate corrected in a staged candidate; not staged into the Windows bridge.
findings.resolving_experiment: Done: reference-rate candidate measured on the attract census, 18 2P pairs and four 1P cases; see resolution.
